findings.reason: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: config->desc.bNumInterfaces and the config->interface[] array contents are declared by the physically attacker-controlled USB device at enumeration (usb core kcallocs the interface pointer array to the device-declared count; entries beyond it are NULL), plus the device-sent HID wireless-status report that schedules wacom->wireless_work (INIT_WORK at wacom_sys.c:2780). MISSING GUARANTEE: grep of drivers/hid/wacom_sys.c shows no bNumInterfaces check anywhere; wacom_wireless_work (2437) immediately indexes usbdev->config->interface[1] (2458) and [2] (2464) with model-assumed fixed indices for the stylus and touch interfaces of a Wacom wireless receiver. UNSAFE USE: usb_get_intfdata(NULL) -> dev_get_drvdata(&intf->dev) reads through a near-NULL pointer, and hid_get_drvdata/wacom_release_resources then operate on the NULL-derived hdev, so a spoofed Wacom wireless-receiver gadget declaring fewer than 3 interfaces plus one device-supplied wireless report crashes the kernel (NULL-page deref, local DoS triggered by plug-in/report, no privileges needed). COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: this is the same code reported as f037 in snapshot s09; the binding is gated on Wacom receiver VID/PIDs, and the work only runs when the HID report parser in wacom_wac.c schedules it, but neither condition constrains bNumInterfaces; the trigger parse itself was not line-re-verified in s12 (kept at medium confidence).
findings.conclusion: wacom_wireless_work indexes usbdev->config->interface[1]/[2] with no bNumInterfaces check; a spoofed Wacom wireless-receiver gadget with <3 interfaces NULL-derefs usb_get_intfdata when a device-sent wireless report runs the work, local DoS.

limitations: The wacom trigger path from a device-sent HID wireless-status report to schedule_work(wacom->wireless_work) in drivers/hid/wacom_wac.c was not re-verified line-by-line in s12; the finding rests on the INIT_WORK site (wacom_sys.c:2780), the unguarded interface[1]/[2] derefs, and identical code to the s09 f037 finding — hence medium, not high, confidence.
Probe-time .endpoint[k] accesses under drivers/media/usb and drivers/net/usb were excluded per branch ownership; they were audited by intents i046/i047 (f045/f046) in this same snapshot.
USB gadget/composite.c config->interface[] indexing was excluded as device-side code where the host is the attacker direction, per branch definition and prior facts.
